definitions.explanation: Bleeding from the nose. A common minor condition, especially in children.

examples.japanese: {鼻血|はなぢ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}た→出る：00513_deru⟧。
{子|こ}ども⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{鼻血|はなぢ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}した→出す：01087_dasu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦ティッシュ→ティッシュ：08816_tisshu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{渡|わた}した→渡す：02442_watasu⟧。
examples.english: The child got a nosebleed, so I gave them a tissue.

examples.japanese: ⟦{乾燥|かんそう}→乾燥：00184_kansou⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{季節|きせつ}→季節：01304_kisetsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{鼻血|はなぢ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}→出る：00513_deru⟧やすい⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{加湿器|かしつき}→加湿器：06491_kashitsuki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧よい。
examples.english: Nosebleeds happen more easily in the dry season, so it's good to use a humidifier.

notes:
USAGE:
The most common pattern is {鼻血|はなぢ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧ (to get a nosebleed, literally "a nosebleed comes out"). The transitive form {鼻血|はなぢ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧ (to produce a nosebleed) is used when describing someone else's nosebleed or an action causing one.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鼻血|はなぢ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧ (to have a nosebleed)
- {鼻血|はなぢ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧ (to get/cause a nosebleed)
- {鼻血|はなぢ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{止|と}まらない→止まる：00555_tomaru⟧ (the nosebleed won't stop)
- {鼻血|はなぢ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{拭|ふ}く→拭く：04261_fuku⟧ (to wipe a nosebleed)

SPELLING NOTE:
The reading is はなぢ (with ぢ), not はなじ. This is because the second element is ⟦{血|ち}→血：01659_chi⟧ (blood), which becomes voiced (ぢ) in compound words through rendaku.
